decisions.mark: explains that a code carries TWO layers — a high-level module part and a low-level part — and that mbedtls_strerror renders both, joined, when both are present
decisions.detail: QUOTE: The bit layout is in `include/mbedtls/error.h:18-40`: a 16-bit code is a sign bit, a 3-bit high-level module ID, a 5-bit module-specific code, and a 7-bit low-level code. A PK error like `-0x3E80` falls entirely in the high-level half, so it gets the high-level string only. A code like `-0x0002` is low-level only.
